passage: Deepak had written his proposal on a page, and after dinner in the courtyard he read it out to his parents. "Saturday I'd like to go to Gopika's house until eight. I'll give you the address and share my location on the phone. I'll call when I arrive, and one of you picks me up at eight. Let's try it for one month, then we talk." Amma looked at Papa. "Gopika's mother will be home?" "Yes. I'll ask her to speak to you." Papa tapped the page. "The month starts this Saturday. If any part is skipped, we stop." "Deal," said Deepak. His palms were damp. On Saturday he called from the gate, and at eight sharp Papa was outside Gopika's house on the scooter, waving.

qa.q: Until what time did Deepak want to stay at Gopika's house?
qa.a: Deepak wanted to stay until eight.

qa.q: How did Deepak feel while reading the proposal aloud?
qa.a: Deepak was nervous but hopeful; the damp palms show the nerves, and the written page shows how much he wanted it to work.

qa.q: What could Deepak offer if a parent still hesitated, and why?
qa.a: Deepak could offer a shorter first visit or have Gopika's mother phone as well, because extra safeguards answer the worry without ending the trial.

qa.q: How might Papa see the proposal?
qa.a: Papa likely feels reassured, since it covers the address, the call on arrival and the pick-up, and a one-month trial lets him check it works.

grounding: The teen proposes going to a friend's house until 8 pm, sharing the address and location, phoning on arrival and being picked up by a parent, offering a one-month trial.

passage: Nadia had been asking to go to Noa's flat after school for weeks, and her mother in Lyon kept saying, "Not yet." So on Sunday Nadia wrote it out and read it at the kitchen table. "Here's my proposal. Fridays only, Noa's flat, until eight. I'll give you the address and share my location. I'll call you when I get there. You or Papa pick me up at eight, no arguing. We try it for a month, and if anything goes wrong, we stop." Her mother looked at the page for a long time. "You've thought about this properly." "I thought about what worries you." Her mother tapped the paper. "One change: I'd like to meet Noa's mother first." "Deal," said Nadia. That Friday she called from Noa's doorstep at 4:15, exactly as promised.

qa.q: Until what time could Nadia stay at Noa's flat?
How might Nadia have felt reading the proposal aloud?
qa.a: She was probably nervous but hopeful, having thought carefully about her mother's worries.

qa.q: Why is the one-month trial a smart part of the proposal?
qa.a: It lets her mother agree without committing forever, and gives Nadia a chance to show she keeps her word.

qa.q: How does Nadia's mother see the proposal?
qa.a: She is impressed that it was thought through, and adds one condition, meeting Noa's mother, before agreeing.

grounding: Shows a teen proposing visits to a friend's flat until eight with address, location sharing, a call on arrival, parent pick-up and a one-month trial.

passage: In the school counsellor's room, Tarun's mother sat stiffly with her handbag on her lap. Hafsa Ma'am nodded at Tarun. "Go on. Tell her what you planned." Tarun unfolded a page. "Mummy, I want to go to Aman's house on Saturdays for the science project. Until eight. Here's his address and his mother's number. I'll share my location the whole time. I'll call when I reach, and you or Papa pick me up at eight. Let's try it for one month. If I'm late even once, we stop." His mother read the page twice. "You wrote all this yourself?" "Hafsa Ma'am only helped me put it in order." She looked at the counsellor, then at him. "One month," she said. "And I'm calling Aman's mother tonight." Tarun grinned. "Deal."

qa.q: Until what time did Tarun ask to stay at Aman's?
What does Tarun's mother sitting stiffly suggest?
qa.a: It suggests she felt tense and wary coming into the meeting, unsure what was being asked.

qa.q: What makes Tarun's proposal a win-win?
qa.a: It gives him Saturdays at Aman's while answering his mother's safety worries with the address, location sharing, a call and pick-up, plus a trial she can end.

qa.q: How does Hafsa Ma'am help without taking over?
qa.a: She encourages Tarun to present it himself and only helped him put it in order, so the plan stays his.

grounding: Shows a teen presenting a conditional one-month trial with address, location sharing, a call on arrival and parent pick-up.
